title: Large Prime Polynomial Correctness
objective: Make GF(p)[x] for p > 2^32-1 Sage-compatible and fast for construction, arithmetic, divrem, gcd, xgcd, factor, roots, evaluation, formatting, and SagePack

handoff.summary: Dense GF(p)[x] now uses canonical BigUint64Array storage for every prime fitting one FLINT word. Wide-prime add, subtract, negate, equality, derivative, evaluation, xgcd, and the already-present multiply/divrem/gcd/factor/roots operations cross generated declared FLINT packed-slice adapters; no polynomial N-API object becomes production state. A SageMath 10.9.post30 oracle at p=2305843009213693951 and an additional prime immediately below 2^64 cover formatting, coefficient iteration, arithmetic, Bezout identities, factors, roots, and SagePack round trips in compiled and dynamic modes. The focused benchmark records 20,000-coefficient construction/add/derivative/evaluation and advanced operation medians.
risks: The declarations are marked wasm=True and portable fallback infrastructure passes, but this lane did not rebuild the FLINT WASM artifact or exercise these seven new symbols in a browser.
Windows x64 and arm64 native builds were not available in this worktree; generated adapters use the existing FLINT word ABI and need normal platform CI.
Current SagePack is correct for wide-prime polynomials but falls back to per-coefficient generic objects: 20,000 coefficients measured 4,178,505 bytes with 78 ms dump and 139 ms load medians.
next_steps: Add canonical fixed-width 8-byte GF(p) polynomial encoding and decoding in tools/serialization.ts; retain deterministic little-endian bytes and reject noncanonical residues.
Rebuild the declared FLINT adapters on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and WebAssembly in the normal platform validation wave.
